_comment: Original practice dialogues written for this app, built around the chapter 1-3 glossary words (not copied from the textbook). Markup in 'fi': [word] marks a glossary word written exactly as in the glossary; [surface](lemma) marks an inflected form, where lemma is the glossary entry. Tapping a marked word shows its meaning and pronunciation.

conversations.title: Uusi kurssi
conversations.subtitle: A new course: greetings, names and spelling

lines.en: Hi! Excuse me, is this seat free?
Yes, it is.
Nice. I'm Sofia.
I'm Leo. Nice to meet you!
Likewise! Is the Finnish course here?
Yes. This is Finnish 1.
Hi, Leo! How are you?
Hey, Matti! Just fine, thanks. And you?
I'm fine.
Hi and welcome! My name is Liisa Virtanen. I'm your teacher.
Excuse me, how is it spelled?
The first name is L-I-I-S-A and the last name V-I-R-T-A-N-E-N.
The course is at 18–20. It ends at 20.
Thank you!

conversations.title: Jäätelökioskilla
conversations.subtitle: At the ice-cream kiosk: prices, spoken numbers, card or cash

lines.en: Hi!
Hi. How much is one scoop?

lines.fi: Yks [pallo] [maksaa] kolme euroo, kaks [palloo](pallo) viis euroo.
lines.en: One scoop costs three euros, two scoops five euros.
OK. I'll take one scoop of strawberry.
I'll take two scoops: chocolate and strawberry.
Sure. Anything else?
No, thanks.
Eight euros in total. Cash or card?
By card, please. I'll pay for these.
Do you need a receipt?
No, thanks.
Thanks, Sofia! Next time I'll pay.

conversations.title: Mistä sinä olet kotoisin?
conversations.subtitle: In the park: countries, languages and getting home

lines.en: Sofia, where are you from?
I'm from Italy. How about you?
I'm Finnish, but my mother is Swedish.
I'm from Canada. My mother tongue is English.
Do you also speak French?
A little. I don't speak French well.
My mother tongue is Italian. What languages do you speak, Matti?
Finnish, Swedish and English.
Where do you live, Leo?
I live in Helsinki. I go home by bus.

lines.fi: [Minä] en asu Helsingissä [vaan](ei X vaan Y) Espoossa. [Minä] [ajan](ajaa) [autolla](auto).
lines.en: I don't live in Helsinki but in Espoo. I drive.
Oh yeah, true! See you tomorrow!

conversations.title: Videopuhelu
conversations.subtitle: A video call with a friend: work, weather and moving

lines.en: Hi, Anni! Are you still sleeping?

lines.fi: En! [Kello] on [jo] [puoli] yhdeksän. [Minun täytyy] [lähteä töihin] pian.
lines.en: No! It's already half past eight. I have to leave for work soon.

lines.fi: [Ai niin, totta]! Sinulla on [uusi] [työpaikka]. [Millainen] se on?
lines.en: Oh right! You have a new job. What is it like?
Really nice. And you? Are you working already?

lines.fi: [Ei vielä]. [Etsin töitä](etsiä töitä), [mutta] se ei ole [helppoa](helppo).
lines.en: Not yet. I'm looking for a job, but it isn't easy.
Now I'm on a Finnish course on Mondays, Wednesdays and Thursdays.
That's great! Your Finnish is already really good.
Thanks, but I don't speak as well as you.
What's the weather like in Rovaniemi?
Quite bad. Only eight degrees. It's raining and windy.

lines.fi: Täällä [aurinko paistaa] [ja] on [lämmin]. Mutta [kesällä](kesä) [yö] on [valoisa], [ja] en [nuku](nukkua) hyvin.
lines.en: Here the sun is shining and it's warm. But in summer the night is bright, and I don't sleep well.
In November it's really dark here. Enjoy the light!
So I hear!
Do you still live in the student apartment?
Yes, but we're moving in September. Our new home is in Vantaa.
Sounds good! Now I have to go. Say hi to Hanna!
Thanks, I'll tell her! Bye bye!

conversations.title: Kurssitoimistossa
conversations.subtitle: At the course office: enrolling in the next course

lines.en: Hi! Can I help?
Hi. I want to enroll in a Finnish course.
Which level?
Finnish 2. When does the next course start?
Just a moment, I'll check… The next course starts next Monday at 9.

lines.fi: Aamulla? [Se ei käy]. Olen aamulla [töissä](olla töissä).
lines.en: In the morning? That doesn't work. I'm at work in the mornings.
Well, there's also another group: on Mondays and Wednesdays at 18.
Sorry, can you say that again?
On Mondays and Wednesdays, at six in the evening.
Good, that works!
Here's a form. Write your first name, last name and home municipality.
What does "kotikunta" mean?
It means the city where you live.
OK. Ready!
Thanks. Now everything is done. You'll get the invoice by e-mail.
Thanks for the help!
